questions.question: Which example is a physical scientific model?
choices: A scale representation of a watershed
A list of unrecorded guesses
An unrelated decorative object
A conclusion with no supporting explanation

questions.question: What is a mathematical model?
choices: A claim that mathematics removes all uncertainty
A physical replica that must be full-sized
A representation using mathematical relationships
A list containing only instrument names

questions.question: What is a conceptual model?
choices: A measurement of an object's exact mass
A representation of how components and processes relate
A claim that cannot be compared with evidence
A model containing every detail of reality

questions.question: What is a model assumption?
choices: An observed fact that can never change
The final answer in every investigation
An instrument's serial number
A condition or simplification accepted for constructing the model

questions.question: What is a model prediction?
choices: A measurement already collected in every case
The model's publication date
An expected outcome derived from the model
A personal preference about a result

questions.question: What does model validation involve?
choices: Making every input equal to zero
Judging only how attractive the model looks
Assuming agreement without testing
Comparing model performance with relevant independent observations

questions.question: What is a simulation?
choices: A guarantee that no measurement error exists
A representation that imitates a system's behavior over time or under conditions
A complete replacement for all observations
A classification rank

questions.question: Why do models simplify real systems?
choices: They emphasize useful features while making analysis manageable
They must omit every important process
They eliminate the need for evidence
They prove systems have only one component

questions.question: Why can two models of the same system both be useful?
choices: They must make identical assumptions
Only the older model can be scientific
They may address different questions or levels of detail
Neither can be compared with observations

questions.question: Why should a model's applicable range be stated?
choices: Its assumptions may work under some conditions but fail under others
Models work perfectly at every scale
A range specifies only the author's age
Applicable ranges make tests unnecessary

questions.question: How can a model be improved after repeated mismatches with observations?
choices: Remove all observations that disagree
Declare every mismatch irrelevant
Add detail without evaluating its effects
Revise assumptions or relationships and test the revised model

questions.question: Why is a scale-model river not necessarily a perfect replica of real flow?
choices: Water behaves identically at all sizes
Scaling can change relationships among forces and dimensions
Only color matters in fluid motion
Physical models cannot use real water

questions.question: Why can sensitivity analysis help evaluate a model?
choices: It proves all inputs are measured exactly
It reveals how outputs change when inputs or assumptions vary
It forces every prediction to stay constant
It measures only the model's physical weight

questions.question: Why is testing on independent data useful after fitting a model?
choices: It guarantees that the model works forever
It makes the fitting data unnecessary to report
It prevents any further revision
It helps assess performance beyond the data used to tune it

questions.question: How should uncertainty in model inputs be treated?
choices: Consider how it may affect predictions
Assume every input is exact
Replace every uncertain value with zero
Ignore it if the model uses equations

questions.question: A globe preserves Earth's overall shape but omits individual buildings. What is the best assessment?
choices: It cannot be a model because it omits detail
It predicts every building's location exactly
It is useful for some geographic questions but not every question
It is useful only if made at Earth's full size

questions.question: A model assumes constant birth rates, but rates change during a drought. What should be examined?
choices: Whether numbers should be removed entirely
Whether all earlier observations were false
Whether drought can be ignored by definition
Whether the assumption affects the model's predictions

questions.question: Two climate simulations differ when one input changes. What can this comparison help reveal?
choices: The exact future climate without uncertainty
The prediction's sensitivity to that input
Which model is universally correct without testing either one
That observations are unnecessary

questions.question: A model predicts 20 units under tested conditions, while repeated reliable measurements are near 35. What is an appropriate response?
choices: Change measurements to 20
Accept 20 solely because it came from a model
Investigate the mismatch and revise or limit the model as needed
Conclude that all scientific models are useless

questions.question: A traffic model accurately predicts morning congestion but fails during road closures. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Its usefulness depends on whether closure conditions are represented
It must predict every possible traffic condition
All morning predictions must therefore be wrong
It has no assumptions
